new_statements.quote: Apesar de o olutyipungu ser uma língua tonal, tal como a maioria das línguas do grupo bantu, neste trabalho não representamos os tons.
new_statements.translation: Although Olutyipungu is a tonal language, like most languages of the Bantu group, in this work we do not represent the tones.
new_statements.citation: Nambalo, Hilário Sabonete. 2021. Aspetos da morfologia e da sintaxe do Olutyipungu (R.12I). MA thesis, Universidade de Lisboa.

Quote: text l.481-482, on the page numbered 15 (form-feed count = p.15), end of sec. 1.4 Metodologia right after conventions (i)-(viii): 'Apesar de o olutyipungu ser uma língua tonal, tal como a maioria das línguas do grupo bantu, neste trabalho não representamo…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (nkhu1238 has no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project). The statement is a tonal-type statement without any word-stress claim, and it is made for Olutyipungu, which Estermann/Lang/da Silva class with olunyaneka/olunkhumbi (p.21: 'não se registando, na sua opinião, diferenças entre o olutyipungu e olunkhumbi') but which the author treats as an autonomous language; Nkhumbi (olunkhumbi) proper is discussed only in the classification chapter 2 (pp.17-23), with no prosodic statement of its own.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The author states only that Olutyipungu (Quipungo variety of the Nyaneka-Nkhumbi cluster) is a tone language and that tones are left unmarked; tone distinguishes the class 1 and class 3 prefixes omù-/omú-. Nothing is said about word stress/accent: a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for acento, acentua*, stress, accent, tónic*, penúltim*, proeminên*, prosód* gives 0 hits, and the thesis has no phonology chapter (morphology ch.3, ditransitive syntax ch.4).
new_statements.identity_note: Nambalo 2021 describes Olutyipungu, the variety of Quipungo municipality (Huíla, Angola), title-page code R.13I (record R.12I), within the Nyaneka-Nkhumbi group; earlier authors (Estermann 1960, Lang 1906, da Silva 1911, Redinha 1974) class it under olunyaneka or olunkhumbi, the author treats it as autonomous. Nkhumbi/olunkhumbi proper (west of Matala, Huíla; north of Ombadja, Cunene) appears only in the ch.2 classification discussion. The tonal statement therefore bears on nkhu1238 only through the cluster-level identification, not as a description of Olunkhumbi itself.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A comparative study of the Bantu and semi-Bantu languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Glottolog 161489)
sources.note: Lu-nkumbi is language no. 92a (Group X, South Angola sub-group) in the comparative vocabularies. The transcription note in the introduction gives only a Bantu-wide convention: 'The accent or pitch of the voice is indicated by \'. This is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception to the prevailing rule in Bantu transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable than the penultimate.' No Nkumbi-specific statement.

sources.note: Dialect Nkumbi-mulondo; 'part of Nyaneka [nyk] cluster, but low intelligibility with the central variants'; Bible portions 1985-1987. No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Jordan, Linda. 2015. A comparison of five speech varieties of southwestern Angola: comparing OluHumbe, OluCilenge, OluKwandu, OluNgendelengo, and OluKuvale in the Kamucuio Municipality, Namibe Province. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-017. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Lexicostatistics, noun classes and segmental correspondences only; 'Tone is not covered in this paper in order to focus on the segmental correspondences' (p. 8). No mention of stress. Her OluHumbe is the Kamucuio (Namibe) Humbe, which she classes as a Nyaneka [nyk] variety, not Nkhumbi [khu].

sources.citation: Melo, Rosa. 2005. «Nyaneka-Nkhumbi»: uma carapuça que não serve aos Handa, nem aos Nyaneka, nem aos Nkhumbi. Cadernos de Estudos Africanos 7/8: 157-178. doi:10.4000/cea.1074
sources.note: Ethnographic/onomastic argument that Handa, Nyaneka and Nkhumbi are distinct groups speaking distinct languages; no phonological content and no linguistic sources on Olunkhumbi in its bibliography.

sources.citation: Nurse, Derek & Gérard Philippson (eds.). 2003. The Bantu Languages. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Nkhumbi (R14) is named only in a pre-prefix remark and in the Herero chapter's subgrouping note (p. 571); nothing on its prosody.

sources.citation: Homburger, L[ilias]. 1925. Le groupe sud-ouest des langues bantoues. Mission Rohan-Chabot, Angola et Rhodesia (1912-1914), Tome III, fasc. 1: Linguistique. Paris: Imprimerie Nationale.
sources.note: Humbe appears only in the survey of peoples (p. 18: 'Les dialectes de Quipungo et de Humbe auraient le même système morphologique que le nyaneka') and in a Kwambi text naming the Nkumbi; no Nkhumbi data and no accent statement for it.

sources.citation: Pereira do Nascimento, José. 1894. Grammatica do Umbundu ou lingua de Benguella. Lisboa: Imprensa Nacional.
sources.note: Names lu-nkumbi as Umbundu's southern neighbour and calls Nogueira's work a 'vocabulário precioso, mas desacompanhado das indispensáveis regras grammaticaes'; nothing on Nkumbi prosody.

sources.citation: Nogueira, António Francisco. 1885. O lu'n kunbi: dialecto do grupo o'n bundo que se falla no interior de Mossamedes. Boletim da Sociedade de Geographia de Lisboa, 5.ª série, pp. 175-262. (Glottolog 164121)
sources.note: Essay on the language (pp. 175-211: prefixes, the nasal element, remarks on its 'sonoridade' — interrogatives 'se assentuam em modulações verdadeiramente musicaes', p. 192) plus a Portuguese–lu'n kunbi vocabulary (pp. 212-262). The only orthographic note (footnote p. 212, verified on the page scan) covers g, n, h, r, s, x and says nothing about accent, stress, tone or length. Vocabulary forms carry acute accents (ongáma, icúla, béro, pútu, condacána, mána) but no placement rule is stated anywhere. Silent on stress.
